{{Short description|English geometer}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''Edward Kingsley Wakeford''' ('''E. K. Wakeford'''; 15 June 1894 – 26 July 1916) was an English geometer.

Born at [[Plymouth, England]], the son of Edward W. Wakeford of [[Gibraltar]], E. K. was educated at [[Borden Grammar School]] and [[Clifton College]] then entered [[Trinity College, Cambridge]] with a mathematics scholarship in 1912.<ref name=cr38/> As a scholar of mathematics, he extended the work of the English mathematician [[James Joseph Sylvester]] (1814–1897) on canonical binary forms for odd degrees, solving the forms for even degrees.<ref name=newman2000/><ref name=bell1986/>  At the time, he was recognized by some mathematicians as a future leader in the field of geometry.<ref name=nature98_321/> In September 1914 he was commissioned in the [[Leicestershire Regiment]] of the [[British Army]] and served during [[World War I]]. On 26 July 1916 he was killed in action on the [[Western Front (World War 1)|Western Front]].<ref name=cr38/>

==Bibliography==
* ''Miquel's theorem and the double six'', Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society, 1918.
* ''Apolarity and canonical forms'', Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society, 1918.
* ''On canonical forms'', Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society, 1920.
* ''Chords of twisted cubics'', Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society, 1923.
